from solution import maximize_elements


def test_issue_example_from_description():
    """Element-wise maximum matches the example in the issue."""
    result = maximize_elements(((1, 3), (4, 5), (2, 9), (1, 10)), ((6, 7), (3, 9), (1, 1), (7, 3)))
    expected = ((6, 7), (4, 9), (2, 9), (7, 10))  # max(1,6)=6,max(3,7)=7; max(4,3)=4,max(5,9)=9; max(2,1)=2,max(9,1)=9; max(1,7)=7,max(10,3)=10
    assert result == expected


def test_issue_first_input_dominates():
    """Maximum picks the first input when all its values are larger."""
    result = maximize_elements(((9, 8), (7, 6)), ((1, 2), (3, 4)))
    expected = ((9, 8), (7, 6))  # max(9,1)=9,max(8,2)=8; max(7,3)=7,max(6,4)=6
    assert result == expected


def test_issue_second_input_dominates():
    """Maximum picks the second input when all its values are larger."""
    result = maximize_elements(((1, 2), (3, 4)), ((9, 8), (7, 6)))
    expected = ((9, 8), (7, 6))  # max(1,9)=9,max(2,8)=8; max(3,7)=7,max(4,6)=6
    assert result == expected


def test_issue_split_winners_need_elementwise_max():
    """Maximum is element-wise, not lexicographic tuple maximum."""
    result = maximize_elements(((1, 10),), ((7, 3),))
    expected = ((7, 10),)  # max(1,7)=7, max(10,3)=10
    assert result == expected


def test_issue_equal_values_stay_same():
    """Maximum of equal values equals that value."""
    result = maximize_elements(((2, 5),), ((2, 5),))
    expected = ((2, 5),)  # max(2,2)=2, max(5,5)=5
    assert result == expected


def test_issue_negative_values():
    """Maximum works for negative numbers."""
    result = maximize_elements(((-5, -1),), ((-3, -10),))
    expected = ((-3, -1),)  # max(-5,-3)=-3, max(-1,-10)=-1
    assert result == expected


def test_issue_zero_boundary():
    """Maximum handles zero against positive and negative boundaries."""
    result = maximize_elements(((0, -2),), ((-1, 0),))
    expected = ((0, 0),)  # max(0,-1)=0, max(-2,0)=0
    assert result == expected


def test_issue_empty_inputs():
    """Maximizing two empty tuples gives an empty tuple."""
    result = maximize_elements((), ())
    expected = ()  # no pairs so no maxima
    assert result == expected


def test_issue_single_pair_consecutive_values():
    """Maximum picks the just-above value for consecutive integers."""
    result = maximize_elements(((5, 6),), ((6, 5),))
    expected = ((6, 6),)  # max(5,6)=6, max(6,5)=6
    assert result == expected


def test_contract_result_is_tuple():
    """Result is a tuple as shown in the example."""
    result = maximize_elements(((1, 3),), ((6, 7),))
    expected = ((6, 7),)  # max(1,6)=6, max(3,7)=7
    assert isinstance(result, tuple) and result == expected


def test_contract_inner_items_are_tuples():
    """Inner items are tuples as shown in the example."""
    result = maximize_elements(((4, 5),), ((3, 9),))
    expected = ((4, 9),)  # max(4,3)=4, max(5,9)=9
    assert isinstance(result[0], tuple) and result == expected


def test_contract_length_matches_inputs():
    """Result length equals input length as shown in the example."""
    result = maximize_elements(((1, 3), (4, 5)), ((6, 7), (3, 9)))
    expected = ((6, 7), (4, 9))  # max(1,6)=6,max(3,7)=7; max(4,3)=4,max(5,9)=9
    assert len(result) == 2 and result == expected
